Source: every paper has at least \% and \&; \_ in identifiers like
"learning\_rate" is universal.
Construct: \$ \% \# \_ \& escapes → literal character in markdown.
Note: bare $ # _ are technically markdown-significant in some positions
but CommonMark only treats them as syntax in restricted contexts (e.g.
# only at start-of-line, _ only between non-word chars). Inline literal
output is the right answer.
Bug-finder: classic source of escape bugs (\$ → \\$, \_ → backslash-underscore).
